learn.rule: An appositive renames a noun. Put it right next to that noun and set it off with commas.
learn.ruleEs: Un appositive (aposición) renombra un sustantivo. Ponlo justo al lado de ese sustantivo y enciérralo entre comas.
learn.model: Jupiter, the largest planet, has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot.
learn.notice: The phrase the largest planet renames Jupiter. It sits between two commas.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses an appositive to rename Mars?

options.text: Mars is called the Red Planet.
Mars the Red Planet is covered in rusty dust.
Mars, the Red Planet, is covered in rusty dust.

items.why: The Red Planet renames Mars and has a comma on each side. The other choices have no commas around a renaming phrase.
items.whyEs: The Red Planet renombra a Mars y tiene una coma a cada lado. Las otras opciones no tienen comas alrededor de una frase que renombra.

items.prompt: Which appositive fits best in this sentence about Saturn?
items.text: Saturn, ____, has rings made of ice and rock.

options.text: spins around very fast
the sixth planet from the Sun
because it has pretty rings

items.why: The sixth planet from the Sun renames Saturn. The other choices do not rename it.
items.whyEs: The sixth planet from the Sun renombra a Saturn. Las otras opciones no lo renombran.

items.prompt: Choose the version with the correct commas around the appositive about Earth.
parts: is the only planet known to have liquid water on its surface.
items.model: Earth, our home planet, is the only planet known to have liquid water on its surface.
items.why: An appositive needs a comma before and after it. Only one choice has both.
items.whyEs: Un appositive necesita una coma antes y otra después. Solo una opción tiene las dos.

items.prompt: Check every space sentence with correct commas around the appositive.

options.text: Neptune the farthest planet from the Sun is very cold.
Venus, the hottest planet, is covered in thick clouds.
The Moon, Earth's only natural satellite, orbits our planet every month.
Mercury, the smallest planet has no moons.

items.why: Look for a comma on both sides of the renaming phrase. Missing either comma makes the sentence incorrect.
items.whyEs: Busca una coma a ambos lados de la frase que renombra. Si falta alguna coma, la oración es incorrecta.

items.prompt: Which sentence about Dr. Rivera puts the appositive next to the noun it renames?

options.text: Dr. Rivera studied the comet, an astronomer, at night.
An astronomer studied, Dr. Rivera, the comet at night.
Dr. Rivera, an astronomer, studied the comet at night.

items.why: An astronomer renames Dr. Rivera, so it belongs right after that name.
items.whyEs: An astronomer renombra a Dr. Rivera, así que va justo después de ese nombre.

items.prompt: Choose the appositive that renames the Sun.

options: , shines at the center of our solar system,
, because it is at the center,
, a star at the center of our solar system,
parts.answer: , a star at the center of our solar system,

items.model: The Sun, a star at the center of our solar system, gives Earth light and heat.
items.why: A star at the center of our solar system renames the Sun. The other choices tell what the Sun does or why.
items.whyEs: A star at the center of our solar system renombra al Sol. Las otras opciones dicen qué hace el Sol o por qué.

write.prompt: Add an appositive to this sentence. Tell more about the cheetah, and put commas on both sides.
write.promptEs: Agrega un appositive a esta oración. Cuenta más sobre el guepardo y pon comas a ambos lados.
write.text: The cheetah runs faster than any other land animal.
write.frame: The cheetah, ___, runs faster than any other land animal.

label: I added a phrase between two commas
Agregué una frase entre dos comas

write.model: The cheetah, a big cat of the African grasslands, runs faster than any other land animal.

familyTalk.en: Say a family member's name, then a phrase that renames them: 'My uncle, ..., lives in ...'.
familyTalk.es: Digan el nombre de un familiar y luego una frase que lo renombre: 'Mi tío, ..., vive en ...'.

teacherTip.en: Show how the sentence still makes sense if you cover the appositive; that is the test for a correct appositive.
teacherTip.es: Muestra que la oración sigue teniendo sentido si tapas el appositive; esa es la prueba de un appositive correcto.

Benjamin Banneker, published almanacs, a self-taught mathematician.

items.prompt: Which appositive fits best in this sentence about Egypt?
items.text: Cairo, ____, sits on the banks of the Nile River.

options.text: next to the desert
because it is a big city
the capital of Egypt

items.why: The capital of Egypt renames Cairo. Next to the desert only tells where.

items.prompt: Choose the version with the correct commas around the appositive about the Great Wall.

options: , a long barrier built across northern China,
, a long barrier built across northern China
a long barrier built across northern China,
parts.answer: , a long barrier built across northern China,

parts: was built to protect people from invaders.
items.model: The Great Wall, a long barrier built across northern China, was built to protect people from invaders.
items.why: Both commas must be there. One before and one after set the appositive apart.
items.whyEs: Deben estar las dos comas. Una antes y otra después separan el appositive.

items.prompt: Check every history sentence with correct commas around the appositive.

options.text: Sacagawea, a Shoshone guide, helped Lewis and Clark on their journey.
The Statue of Liberty a gift from France stands in New York Harbor.
Ms. Garcia, our social studies teacher, showed us a map of Mali.
Lin, my classmate presented a report on Marco Polo.

items.why: Each correct sentence has a comma before and after the phrase that renames the noun.
items.whyEs: Cada oración correcta tiene una coma antes y otra después de la frase que renombra el sustantivo.

items.prompt: Which sentence about Marco Polo puts the appositive next to the noun it renames?

options.text: Marco Polo traveled to China, an Italian merchant, in the 1200s.
An Italian merchant traveled, Marco Polo, to China in the 1200s.
Marco Polo, an Italian merchant, traveled to China in the 1200s.

items.why: An Italian merchant renames Marco Polo, so it goes right after his name.
items.whyEs: An Italian merchant renombra a Marco Polo, así que va justo después de su nombre.

items.prompt: Which appositive fits best in this sentence about Mali?

the ruler of the Mali Empire
because he ruled Mali

items.whyEs: The ruler of the Mali Empire renombra a Mansa Musa. Las otras opciones no son nombres para él.

items.prompt: Check every story-world sentence with correct commas around the appositive.
